## `pse`

~~~~text
Native host capabilities; explicit preparation: scripts/bootstrap-host

Usage: pse [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  qualify-study      Run the fixed original Study coordinator in this application scope using prepared images
  search             Find source, text, Rust entities and relationships through one typed query
  inspect            Inspect a known source or an addressed search result without preparation
  propose            Construct a checked change preview from an exact guarded result
  compiler           Explicitly generate selected native compiler evidence or run authored compiler probes
  worktree           Create prepared sibling worktrees or inspect native checkout users
  run-all            Attempt every independent Just recipe under one native foreground owner
  tests              Explicitly build/list the actual selected native test population
  test               Build, execute and reconcile the actual selected native tests
  check              Check the selected source through the correctness and compiler observation owners
  fixture            Prepare or inspect inputs through the existing native fixture owner
  tools              Explicit captured development-tool preparation, discovery and managed native forwarding
  wait               Observe one original managed invocation; an observation timeout leaves it running
  cancel             Stop one authenticated original invocation and inspect its original settlement evidence
  observe            Inspect scientific evidence through an explicitly prepared native product reader
  docs               Forward documentation operations to the explicitly prepared native owner
  api                Explicitly acquire Rust API artifacts, run compatibility rules or check documentation
  code               Explicitly prepare, observe or settle a native Rust semantic session
  probe              Create and run an explicitly isolated authored Rust experiment
  commands           Discover actual command declarations or lazily query one argument's candidates
  help               Inspect one command's native help and public parser metadata
  status             Read independent native checkout, invocation and prepared-tool observations
  schema             Print the serialization schema of a command's actual detail view
  doctor
  cargo-tools
  diagnostic-tools
  telemetry-service
  native
  server
  study-module
  env
  activity
  history            Inspect newest invocation metadata without reading historical result payloads
  run

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --version


  -h, --help
~~~~

## `pse search`

~~~~text
Find source, text, Rust entities and relationships through one typed query

Usage: pse search [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  schema      Search declarations in an explicitly selected complete descriptor set
  files       Discover selected files and their source kinds
  text        Search native text, preserving byte and encoding policies
  syntax      Match a native Rust syntax pattern or explicit Tree-sitter extraction query
  symbol      Find written declarations or explicitly selected semantic workspace symbols
  api         Search an explicitly acquired native API artifact without acquisition
  structured  Select a structured field using a typed JSON Pointer
  history     Investigate native Git history without changing the checkout

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --request <REQUEST>
          Read a complete typed JSON request; explicit flags override selected fields

      --config <CONFIG>
          Explicit named-query configuration; otherwise use the optional repository file

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --query <QUERY>
          Select a saved typed query from configuration

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --path <PATHS>
          Restrict source paths without requiring Cargo or analyzer preparation

      --package <PACKAGE>


      --glob <GLOB>


      --exclude <EXCLUDE>


      --type <TYPES>


      --tracked


      --untracked


      --changed


      --dependencies


      --include-ignored


      --hidden


      --generated


      --index


      --revision <REVISION>


      --limit <LIMIT>
          Stop after this many useful results; the default is twenty

      --all
          Examine the complete selected scope instead of using the default result limit

      --exists
          Stop after a positive witness; a negative answer requires complete examination

      --count


      --count-unit <COUNT_UNIT>
          Select the population counted by an explicit count demand

          [possible values: matches, files, lines, entities]

      --order <ORDER>
          [possible values: arrival, deterministic]

      --cursor <CURSOR>
          Continue a deterministic page under its original query/source guards

      --result-fields <RESULT_FIELDS>
          Select result detail fields; source identity and coverage remain mandatory

      --group-by <GROUP_BY>
          Group returned witnesses, without claiming exhaustive group counts

          [possible values: source, kind, name]

      --explain
          Explain the effective validated query without invoking its providers

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
~~~~

## `pse propose`

~~~~text
Construct a checked change preview from an exact guarded result

Usage: pse propose [OPTIONS]
       pse propose <COMMAND>

Commands:
  grammar      Grammar-aware Rust edits at an exact native node, without semantic preparation
  rename       Preview only the selected entity's native semantic rename; no source writes
  file-rename  Preview native file-rename follow-up edits and the exact filesystem operation
  assists      Enumerate native assists without eagerly resolving every edit
  assist       Resolve one source/generation-bound native assist into an immutable proposal
  ssr          Preview the native semantic SSR rule (PATTERN ==>> REPLACEMENT), scoped to selected lines
  syntax       Native capture-preserving syntax template, not literal replacement text

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --result <RESULT>
          Original result reference as returned JSON or its portable encoded form

      --replacement <REPLACEMENT>
          Exact replacement preview; source and index remain untouched

      --rename <RENAME>
          Native semantic rename preview, requiring the original provider context

      --file-rename <FILE_RENAME>


      --ssr <SSR>


      --assist <ASSIST>


      --assists
~~~~

## `pse propose grammar`

~~~~text
Grammar-aware Rust edits at an exact native node, without semantic preparation

Usage: pse propose grammar [OPTIONS] --byte-start <BYTE_START> --byte-end <BYTE_END> <FILE> <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add-where     Append a written where predicate; necessity and deduplication are not inferred
  remove-use    Remove the selected grouped import branch, settling empty parents and separators
  remove-bound  Remove the selected type bound and its separator
  insert-item   Append one associated item to a selected impl/trait body
  insert-field  Append one named field to a selected record declaration
  expression    Construct a binary expression with parenthesized operands and result

Arguments:
~~~~

## `pse propose syntax`

~~~~text
Native capture-preserving syntax template, not literal replacement text

Usage: pse propose syntax [OPTIONS] --pattern <PATTERN> --replacement <REPLACEMENT> <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...
          Exact source operands, acquired independently without a semantic session

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --pattern <PATTERN>
          Native code-shaped Rust pattern ($NAME or $$$SEQUENCE captures)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --strictness <STRICTNESS>
          Possible values:
          - cst:       Match all concrete syntax nodes
          - smart:     Native smart policy, retaining significant written syntax
          - ast:       Match named AST nodes
          - relaxed:   Ignore comments and unnamed punctuation
          - signature: Compare structural signatures without terminal text
          - template:  Native textual template matching policy

          [default: smart]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --inside <INSIDE>
          Require an ancestor matching each native pattern

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --has <HAS>
          Require a proper descendant matching each native pattern

      --exclude <EXCLUDE>
          Exclude a candidate matching any of these native patterns

      --capture <CAPTURE>
          Extract only this named capture (without sigils); absence retains all captures

      --index
          Read the raw staging-index blob rather than working bytes

      --revision <REVISION>
          Read a committed blob; resolve the revision before returning its identity

      --language <LANGUAGE>
          Override the .rs/.md/.markdown filename inference

          Possible values:
          - rust:     Lossless Rust syntax, without Cargo/cfg/macro expansion
          - markdown: CommonMark headings and their source sections

      --edition <EDITION>
          Explicit syntax policy; no Cargo edition or cfg discovery is performed

          Possible values:
          - 2015: Rust 2015 syntax
          - 2018: Rust 2018 syntax
          - 2021: Rust 2021 syntax
          - 2024: Rust 2024 syntax

          [default: 2024]

      --replacement <REPLACEMENT>


      --select <SELECTED>
          Select candidate indices; absence retains candidates without choosing edits

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse compiler generate`

~~~~text
Explicitly generate native selected-unit/body artifacts through correctness admission

Usage: pse compiler generate [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> --question <QUESTION> <PACKAGE>

Arguments:
  <PACKAGE>
          One Cargo package; default target is its library unless --bin is selected

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --kind <KIND>
          Possible values:
          - mir:        Body/pass-filtered MIR before/after files
          - facts:      Owned typed capture, suspension and cleanup observations from the pinned compiler
          - thir:       Selected unit THIR debug text; native rustc has no body filter for this view
          - type-sizes: Selected unit encountered concrete layouts; no cross-target ABI conclusion
          - mono-items: Selected unit monomorphization collection, separate from runtime reach
          - evaluate:   Authored isolated probe evaluation; stdout meaning belongs to its source

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --question <QUESTION>
          Original investigation question, retained without inferring an answer

      --body <BODY>
          MIR substring, or exact owning body path for facts (including nested closures/coroutines)

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --fact-focus <FACT_FOCUS>
          Native query family for typed facts; other artifact kinds require the all default

          Possible values:
          - all:        Acquire all supported families within the selected owning body
          - captures:   Capture places, types, modes and source causes
          - suspension: Saved coroutine fields and their suspension variants
          - cleanup:    Analysis initialization and lowered normal/unwind cleanup

          [default: all]

      --pass <PASSES>
          Native MIR pass substrings; select before/after artifacts at their actual phase

      --bin <BIN>


      --lib


      --target <TARGET>
          Explicit Cargo target; no component is installed automatically

      --all-features
          Activate all available features

      --no-default-features
          Do not activate the `default` feature

  -F, --features <FEATURES>
          Space-separated list of features to activate

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

~~~~text
Explicitly build/list the actual selected native test population

Arguments:

Options:

      --changed
          Conservatively select changed source owners and reverse dependencies

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --base <BASE>
          Git base for --changed, including observed index/worktree/untracked changes

          [default: HEAD]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

  -p, --package <SPEC>
          Package to process (see `cargo help pkgid`)

      --workspace
          Process all packages in the workspace

      --exclude <SPEC>
          Exclude packages from being processed

      --all-features
          Activate all available features

      --no-default-features
          Do not activate the `default` feature

  -F, --features <FEATURES>
          Space-separated list of features to activate

      --lib
          Select actual library declarations, without guessing their names

      --all-targets
          Preserve native Cargo all-targets selection without enabling all features

      --test <TEST_TARGET>
          Select one integration-test target

      --bin <BIN_TARGET>
          Select one binary target

      --without-feature <ABSENT>
          Features that the actual selected compiler roots must keep absent

      --target <PLATFORM>
          Explicit Cargo target platform; host dependency contexts remain independent

      --target-kind <TARGET_KIND>
          Disambiguate duplicate target names by their Cargo kind, for example test or bin

      --ignore-default-filter
          Bypass the selected nextest profile's default filter

  -E, --filterset <EXPRESSIONS>
          Native nextest filtersets; nextest owns their grammar

      --ignored <IGNORED>
          Possible values:
          - default: Run ordinary tests only
          - only:    Run ignored tests only
          - all:     Run ordinary and ignored tests

          [default: default]

      --profile <PROFILE>
          Selected nextest policy profile, without running its setup during explain

          [default: default]

      --timings
          Ask native Cargo for timing diagnostics (shared mutable output, not retained evidence)

      --detach
          Return the original managed launch identity and leave its owner running

      --session <SESSION>
          Correlate this operation with an agent session without granting control authority

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
~~~~

~~~~text
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --samples <SAMPLES>
          Maximum whole snapshots emitted before observation stops

          [default: 32]

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --interval-ms <INTERVAL_MS>
          Minimum polling interval; native progress never awaits this renderer

          [default: 1000]

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          Observer allowance; its expiry does not time out the original workload

          [default: 30]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse api`

~~~~text
Explicitly acquire Rust API artifacts, run compatibility rules or check documentation

Usage: pse api [OPTIONS] <--prepare|--compatibility|--check-docs|--extract-examples> <CRATE_QUERY> [PATH]

Arguments:
  <CRATE_QUERY>
          Exact locked dependency name, name@version or source-qualified Cargo package ID

  [PATH]
          Public crate-relative item path; omission lists candidates

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --export-jsonl <EXPORT_JSONL>
          Export deterministic JSONL facts from an already acquired artifact into a new directory

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --search <SEARCH>
          Case-insensitive name/documentation search

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --target <TARGET>
          Explicit target triple; default is the pinned rustc's observed host

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --kind <KIND>
          Possible values:
          - function:   A free or associated function
          - struct:     A struct declaration
          - enum:       An enum declaration
          - union:      A union declaration
          - trait:      A trait or trait alias
          - type-alias: A type alias
          - constant:   A constant or associated constant
          - static:     A static declaration
          - module:     A module declaration
          - macro:      A declarative or procedural macro
          - other:      Another rustdoc declaration, retained without guessing its kind

      --input <INPUT>


      --where <WHERE_SHAPES>
          Structural declared where predicate; may be repeated

      --output-type <OUTPUT_TYPE>


      --trait-name <TRAIT_NAME>


      --unsafe-only


      --async-only


      --const-only


      --docs
          Expand authored documentation for returned candidates

      --examples
          Expand authored Rust examples and hidden setup; never execute them

      --native-examples <NATIVE_EXAMPLES>
          Inspect an explicitly acquired doctests.json, preserving native transformations

      --declaration
          Expand the original format-qualified rustdoc item, including complex bounds/associated data

      --adjacency <ADJACENCY>
          Examine selected declared adjacency; never acquires an analyzer or another artifact

          Possible values:
          - contains:           Declared child/associated item
          - bound:              Explicit supertrait or structured declared bound
          - implementation:     An impl record, without a use-site applicability verdict
          - provided-default:   Default trait method supplied by an impl's recorded provided-method list
          - reexport:           Public facade to its definition
          - documentation-link: Compiler-resolved intra-documentation link

      --compare-with <COMPARE_WITH>
          Read structural differences from an explicitly selected acquired document.json; --compatibility separately executes native rules. Neither generates an input

      --cursor <CURSOR>
          Continue the same immutable artifact/query page; stale contexts refuse

      --prepare
          Explicitly acquire documentation; passive reads use inspect api

      --compatibility
          Explicitly execute separately prepared compatibility rules

      --check-docs
          Explicitly check workspace library documentation through native rustdoc

      --extract-examples
          Explicitly preprocess native doctests to format2; no examples compile or run

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse inspect`

~~~~text
Inspect a known source or an addressed search result without preparation

Usage: pse inspect [OPTIONS] <--result <RESULT>|--source <SOURCE>>
       pse inspect <COMMAND>

Commands:
  dependency-usage    Observe written references to exact Cargo package IDs in a prepared native world
  comparison          Compare explicitly addressed source, API, retained context or native world evidence
  schema              Navigate an explicitly supplied complete descriptor set, or compare schema worlds
  payload             Explain selected binary, JSON or textproto payloads without invoking an RPC
  developer-evidence  Export source-generated observations from original private workflow evidence
  outline             Read written declarations or document headings without semantic preparation
  declaration         Read a known declaration, literal item, position or exact original range
  origin              Inspect the declared authored owner of an exact generated-source hit
  entity              Inspect a known Rust position through its explicitly prepared native semantic owner
  api                 Inspect an exact locked API, original docs/examples, reexports or structural differences
  dependency          Inspect native exact dependency identity, features and inclusion explanations
  dependency-units    Inspect planned compiler units without building or listing tests
  owner               Inspect existing source, generated and document ownership independently
  diagnostic          Read original compiler failures or one addressed original record
  artifact            Read exact artifact ranges with native validators; this does not decode a protocol
  compiler-artifact   Read an original native compiler artifact after its existing whole-file verification
  compiler-artifacts  Inspect compiler artifacts, or original admitted check/test/compiler contexts with --metadata
  compiler-source     Read compiler-verified original source bytes from an acquired facts artifact
  compiler-facts      Explain original typed capture, suspension and cleanup observations without rerunning rustc
  tests               Read an already captured original test population or its original failures
  test-selection      Explain real native test selection; no binary listing or test execution occurs
  check-selection     Explain selected native check declarations or admitted compiler units without compiling
  invocation          Read the original managed result without waiting, cancellation or resubmission
  log                 Read original retained stdout/stderr byte ranges
  affected            Explain conservative affected-test reach through the existing native owner
  changes             Inspect native Git layers and source/test ownership without compiling

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --result <RESULT>
          Original result reference: returned JSON object or its portable encoded form

      --source <SOURCE>
          Direct known source: no preliminary search is required

      --index


      --revision <REVISION>


      --range-start <RANGE_START>


      --range-end <RANGE_END>


      --lines <LINES>


      --head <HEAD>


      --tail <TAIL>


      --view <VIEW>
          Expand one selected semantic fact through its original native provider

          Possible values:
          - associations:    Explain qualified source, generator, document and lifecycle connections
          - relevance:       Explain original test/setup/assertion evidence without executing tests
          - adjacency
          - compatibility
          - visibility
          - format-origin
          - derive-origin
          - lifetime
          - declaration
          - layout:          Inspect fallible native layout under the selected semantic world and target
          - references
          - calls
          - implementations
          - macro
          - tests
          - candidates
          - hints
          - hint
          - candidate
          - predicate

      --semantic
          Enrich association/relevance evidence through an explicitly prepared native world

      --adjacency <ADJACENCY>
          Selected acquired-artifact edges for --view adjacency; omission selects all kinds

          Possible values:
          - contains:           Declared child/associated item
          - bound:              Explicit supertrait or structured declared bound
          - implementation:     An impl record, without a use-site applicability verdict
          - provided-default:   Default trait method supplied by an impl's recorded provided-method list
          - reexport:           Public facade to its definition
          - documentation-link: Compiler-resolved intra-documentation link

      --select <SELECT>


      --predicate <PREDICATE>


      --compiler-layout <COMPILER_LAYOUT>
          Passively associate an original type-sizes acquisition with --view layout

      --against-result <AGAINST_RESULT>
          Guarded second operand for compatibility or destination visibility

      --operation <OPERATION>
          Exact native compatibility operation; never inferred from display text

          Possible values:
          - equal:        Exact native type equality in a common owner
          - could-unify:  Possible deep unification, not compiler acceptance
          - could-coerce: Directional possible coercion from selected to against

      --compiler-evidence <COMPILER_EVIDENCE>
          Original compiler facts evidence supplied to a lifetime inquiry

      --work-result <WORK_RESULT>
          Accompanying original work outcome, with association qualified separately

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

~~~~text
          - navigation: Declaration navigation only; facts and decoded mappings are not constructed
          - facts:      Selected original facts and interpreted values, without character mappings
          - mapped:     Selected facts with available decoded-character correspondence

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --item <ITEM>


      --at-byte <AT_BYTE>


      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --at-line <AT_LINE>


      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --at-column <AT_COLUMN>


      --range-start <RANGE_START>


      --range-end <RANGE_END>


      --index
          Read the raw staging-index blob rather than working bytes

      --revision <REVISION>
          Read a committed blob; resolve the revision before returning its identity

      --language <LANGUAGE>
          Override the .rs/.md/.markdown filename inference

          Possible values:
          - rust:     Lossless Rust syntax, without Cargo/cfg/macro expansion
          - markdown: CommonMark headings and their source sections

      --edition <EDITION>
          Explicit syntax policy; no Cargo edition or cfg discovery is performed

          Possible values:
          - 2015: Rust 2015 syntax
          - 2018: Rust 2018 syntax
          - 2021: Rust 2021 syntax
          - 2024: Rust 2024 syntax

          [default: 2024]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

~~~~text
          - symbols
          - refs
          - calls
          - implementations
          - macro
          - tests
          - candidates
          - candidate
          - hints
          - hint
          - predicate
          - assists

          [default: explain]

      --select <SELECT>


      --text <TEXT>


      --compiler-layout <COMPILER_LAYOUT>

      --compiler-evidence <COMPILER_EVIDENCE>
          Original compiler artifact reference accompanying a lifetime inquiry

      --work-result <WORK_RESULT>
          Original work invocation accompanying the inquiry; no execution association is inferred

      --against-result <AGAINST_RESULT>
          Original guarded position for a native compatibility or visibility comparison

      --operation <OPERATION>
          Possible values:
          - equal:        Exact native type equality in a common owner
          - could-unify:  Possible deep unification, not compiler acceptance
          - could-coerce: Directional possible coercion from selected to against

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
~~~~

~~~~text
          [default: auto]

          Case-insensitive name/documentation search

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

      --kind <KIND>

          - function:   A free or associated function
          - struct:     A struct declaration
          - enum:       An enum declaration
          - union:      A union declaration
          - trait:      A trait or trait alias
          - type-alias: A type alias
          - constant:   A constant or associated constant
          - static:     A static declaration
          - module:     A module declaration
          - macro:      A declarative or procedural macro
          - other:      Another rustdoc declaration, retained without guessing its kind

      --input <INPUT>


      --where <WHERE_SHAPES>
          Structural declared where predicate; may be repeated

      --output-type <OUTPUT_TYPE>


      --trait-name <TRAIT_NAME>


      --unsafe-only


      --async-only


      --const-only


      --docs
          Expand authored documentation for returned candidates

      --examples
          Expand authored Rust examples and hidden setup; never execute them

      --native-examples <NATIVE_EXAMPLES>
          Inspect an explicitly acquired doctests.json, preserving native transformations

      --declaration
          Expand the original format-qualified rustdoc item, including complex bounds/associated data

      --adjacency <ADJACENCY>
          Examine selected declared adjacency; never acquires an analyzer or another artifact

          Possible values:
          - contains:           Declared child/associated item
          - bound:              Explicit supertrait or structured declared bound
          - implementation:     An impl record, without a use-site applicability verdict
          - provided-default:   Default trait method supplied by an impl's recorded provided-method list
          - reexport:           Public facade to its definition
          - documentation-link: Compiler-resolved intra-documentation link

      --compare-with <COMPARE_WITH>
          Read structural differences from an explicitly selected acquired document.json; --compatibility separately executes native rules. Neither generates an input

      --cursor <CURSOR>
          Continue the same immutable artifact/query page; stale contexts refuse
~~~~

~~~~text
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse inspect test-selection`

~~~~text
Explain real native test selection; no binary listing or test execution occurs

Usage: pse inspect test-selection [OPTIONS] [PACKAGE[:TARGET]]... [-- <WORDS>...]

Arguments:
  [PACKAGE[:TARGET]]...
          Workspace package names, optionally followed by :TARGET. Use -p for opaque package IDs

  [WORDS]...
          Bare test-name filters after --; these are not package or target names

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --rerun-failed <INVOCATION>
          Rebuild current source for exact failed identities and original compiler policy

      --changed
          Conservatively select changed source owners and reverse dependencies

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --base <BASE>
          Git base for --changed, including observed index/worktree/untracked changes

          [default: HEAD]

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

  -p, --package <SPEC>
          Package to process (see `cargo help pkgid`)

      --workspace
          Process all packages in the workspace

      --exclude <SPEC>
          Exclude packages from being processed

      --all-features
          Activate all available features

      --no-default-features
          Do not activate the `default` feature

  -F, --features <FEATURES>
          Space-separated list of features to activate

      --lib
          Select actual library declarations, without guessing their names

      --all-targets
          Preserve native Cargo all-targets selection without enabling all features

      --test <TEST_TARGET>
          Select one integration-test target

      --bin <BIN_TARGET>
          Select one binary target

      --without-feature <ABSENT>
          Features that the actual selected compiler roots must keep absent

      --target <PLATFORM>
          Explicit Cargo target platform; host dependency contexts remain independent

      --target-kind <TARGET_KIND>
          Disambiguate duplicate target names by their Cargo kind, for example test or bin

      --ignore-default-filter
          Bypass the selected nextest profile's default filter

  -E, --filterset <EXPRESSIONS>
          Native nextest filtersets; nextest owns their grammar

      --ignored <IGNORED>
          Possible values:
          - default: Run ordinary tests only
          - only:    Run ignored tests only
          - all:     Run ordinary and ignored tests

          [default: default]

      --profile <PROFILE>
          Selected nextest policy profile, without running its setup during explain

          [default: default]

      --from-result <FROM_RESULT>
          Validate a source witness, then select its current containing package as a test candidate

      --admitted


      --full


  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

~~~~text
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse inspect dependency`

~~~~text
Inspect native exact dependency identity, features and inclusion explanations

Usage: pse inspect dependency [OPTIONS] <PACKAGE>

Arguments:
  <PACKAGE>


Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --metadata <METADATA>


      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --why


      --feature-member <FEATURE_MEMBER>


      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~

## `pse inspect dependency-units`

~~~~text
Inspect planned compiler units without building or listing tests

Usage: pse inspect dependency-units [OPTIONS] <DEPENDENCY> [PACKAGE[:TARGET]]...

Arguments:
  <DEPENDENCY>


  [PACKAGE[:TARGET]]...
          Workspace package names, optionally followed by :TARGET. Use -p for opaque package IDs

Options:
  -C <checkout>


      --native-world
          Explain qualified correspondence to the explicitly prepared native world

      --format <FORMAT>
          Human output on terminals, JSON on pipes, or compact NDJSON observations

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Human for a terminal, JSON for pipes
          - human:  Concise summary and pretty structured detail
          - json:   One JSON envelope
          - ndjson: Compact normalized records followed by an observation summary

          [env: PSE_FORMAT]
          [default: auto]

      --metadata-original
          Include the original captured metadata alongside the planned-unit explanation

      --changed
          Conservatively select changed source owners and reverse dependencies

      --fields <FIELDS>
          Select comma-separated literal top-level payload names (for example records). Dots and slashes do not navigate nested data; schema shows valid choices

      --base <BASE>
          Git base for --changed, including observed index/worktree/untracked changes

          [default: HEAD]

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Limit whole payload records; producer pages retain their omission and continuation facts

  -p, --package <SPEC>
          Package to process (see `cargo help pkgid`)

      --workspace
          Process all packages in the workspace

      --exclude <SPEC>
          Exclude packages from being processed

      --all-features
          Activate all available features

      --no-default-features
          Do not activate the `default` feature

  -F, --features <FEATURES>
          Space-separated list of features to activate

      --lib
          Select actual library declarations, without guessing their names

      --all-targets
          Preserve native Cargo all-targets selection without enabling all features

      --test <TEST_TARGET>
          Select one integration-test target

      --bin <BIN_TARGET>
          Select one binary target

      --without-feature <ABSENT>
          Features that the actual selected compiler roots must keep absent

      --target <PLATFORM>
          Explicit Cargo target platform; host dependency contexts remain independent

      --target-kind <TARGET_KIND>
          Disambiguate duplicate target names by their Cargo kind, for example test or bin

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

~~~~
